**Tier 4** — decisions — policies, overrides, scenarios · owned by `policy-ui` · `public.policy_presets`

**One row is** One named policy bundle a user can apply to a project — the DECISION plane's catalog of starting points. A system preset (`is_system`) ships with the product; a user preset belongs to its `owner_id`.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `editor` |
| Tier transitions audited | yes |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 5 — **1 with no predicate** |

Tier 4 — the DECISION plane: a preset is a choice a person can make, not a fact about their supply chain. Audited from WP 6.4, with the three statement-grain triggers landing beside this sidecar, because `dataPlaneAudit.test.ts` scopes its rule to tables IN the contract and a deferred table's writes are unaudited with nothing to notice (D54). **`write` is null because NO USER-FACING WRITE PATH EXISTS — and neither does a read path (§4 D126).** The table is granted `SELECT` to `anon` under a permissive policy and nothing in `src/`, in an RPC or in an edge function reads it; the presets a user actually sees come from TypeScript modules under `src/lib/policies/presets/`. So this row's governance describes a table that is reachable and unread, which is a different statement from "restricted", and saying it plainly is the point of the block.

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 1 policy here grants access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `Anon can read policy presets` — `SELECT` to `anon`, `authenticated`
>
> See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.

## Columns

`CSV header` is the name the **user types**, which is not always the column name —
that gap is defect D21. A dash means the column has no CSV origin.

| Column | CSV header | Type | Unit | Required in CSV | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` 🔑 | — | `uuid` | — | — | Surrogate key. The natural key is (slug, owner_id) below. |
| `slug` | — | `text` | — | — | The preset's stable name — `lean_jit`, `make_to_order`. Half the natural key, so one owner may not hold two presets under one slug while two owners may each hold their own. |
| `name` | — | `text` | — | — | What a person reads — "Lean / JIT". The slug is the key; this is the label. |
| `description` | — | `text` | — | — | One sentence on what the preset does to a project. NULL where nobody wrote one; there is no default sentence, because an invented description of a decision is worse than none. |
| `is_system` | — | `boolean` | — | — | TRUE for a preset that ships with the product and FALSE for one a user saved. It is the only thing separating a catalog entry from somebody's own work, and `owner_id` is NULL on the system rows. |
| `owner_id` | — | `uuid` | — | — | The user whose preset this is, or NULL for a system preset. Half the natural key — and the NULL half, which is why the pair behaves the way `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` indexes elsewhere in this contract had to be made to behave (§4 D5): without that, two system presets could share a slug. |
| `bundle` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | THE DECISION ITSELF — a partial policy bundle, keyed by family, merged over a project's defaults when the preset is applied. Partial on purpose: a preset that carried every field would overwrite choices it has no opinion about. |
| `created_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the row was written. Server-stamped, never the client's clock. |
| `updated_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When it was last changed. Maintained by a trigger where one exists; with no writer at all today (D126) it equals `created_at` on every row. |
